tasks.title: Bootstrap the executable monorepo foundation
tasks.objective: Create a minimal installable pnpm monorepo with strict TypeScript, one formatting strategy, root validation scripts, three web app shells, packages, and a Foundry workspace without fictitious contract implementations.
deliverables: Pinned runtime/toolchain policy and package-manager metadata
Root dev, build, lint, typecheck, test, and e2e scripts
Minimal compilable app/package shells and Foundry test harness
acceptance: A clean clone can install with the documented command
Root lint, typecheck, unit tests, builds, and Foundry tests pass
No app requires secrets or network access to validate the baseline
validation: pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build
failureModes: Unsupported Node or pnpm versions fail with an actionable message
Missing optional environment values do not break baseline tests
No empty Solidity contracts are added only to satisfy the target tree

tasks.title: Create the public GitHub repository and governance baseline
tasks.objective: After explicit publication approval, create the public gordo-labs repository, push the reviewed foundation, and configure minimum open-source and security governance.
deliverables: Verified public remote and default branch
CI, dependency update, secret scanning, and private vulnerability reporting configuration
Accurate repository URLs and publication state in project docs
acceptance: Repository visibility is verified as public
CI runs the same required root checks as local development
Secret scan and repository governance settings are recorded
validation: Inspect branch protection and private vulnerability reporting
failureModes: Stop before any external write if approval is absent
Do not weaken security settings merely to make CI green
No secrets, real credentials, or local backups enter Git history

tasks.title: Pin the standards and dependency compatibility baseline
tasks.objective: Re-check official sources, evaluate maintained libraries, and record exact compatible versions and replaceable adapter boundaries before protocol or account code is written.
deliverables: ADR covering toolchain and credential libraries
Compatibility matrix for OpenID4VC, SD-JWT VC, Safe/Kernel, EntryPoint, ERC-7579, browsers, and Foundry
License and maintenance-risk notes for every selected dependency
acceptance: Every unstable standard has an exact pinned revision
Every selected library has license, maintenance, and replacement notes
Known version conflicts and unsupported browsers/chains are explicit
validation: Verify versions against official docs and package registries
Run dependency license and vulnerability reports
failureModes: Reject abandoned or incompatible dependencies
Do not silently mix draft-era and final OpenID4VC field names
Do not treat ERC-7579 or SD-JWT VC as final

tasks.title: Implement shared runtime schemas and DCQL policy mapping
tasks.objective: Define versioned runtime-validated types for internal presentation policies, verification results, credential metadata, and a narrow mapping to and from OpenID4VP 1.0 DCQL.
deliverables: Schemas with unknown-field and size policy
Age-over-18 policy using is_over_18 rather than hidden birthdate comparison
Positive and negative DCQL mapping fixtures
acceptance: Invalid types, operators, paths, and disclosure requests are rejected
Round-trip mappings are deterministic for the supported subset
Schema versions are included in persisted or exchanged project-owned objects
failureModes: Fail closed on unsupported operators or formats
Bound nesting, array counts, and string sizes
Never infer a predicate proof from selective disclosure

tasks.title: Implement nonce, replay, and verification-result domain logic
tasks.objective: Build infrastructure-free challenge generation, state/nonce lifecycle, atomic single-use replay protection, verification-result construction, and stable error codes.
deliverables: Cryptographically strong challenge generator behind an injectable port
TTL-aware atomic replay store interface plus in-memory adapter
Verification pipeline result and failure taxonomy
acceptance: Challenges provide at least 128 bits of entropy
Concurrent reuse consumes a challenge at most once
Expired, wrong-audience, unknown, and reused challenges produce distinct safe errors
validation: Unit and concurrency tests with deterministic clock/random ports
Property tests for challenge encoding and TTL boundaries
failureModes: Never log raw presentation tokens or secrets
Clock skew policy is explicit and bounded
Storage failure cannot turn a rejected replay into acceptance

tasks.title: Design and prove the vault key-management boundary
tasks.objective: Decide and prototype versioned vault key wrapping for WebAuthn PRF-capable and non-PRF browsers without treating a passkey signature as encryption material.
deliverables: ADR for data-encryption keys, wrapping keys, salts, KDF parameters, and recovery factors
Capability-detection prototype for WebAuthn PRF
Deterministic crypto test vectors and migration envelope
acceptance: PRF absence has a documented secure fallback
No wrapping key or recovery secret is persisted plaintext
Backup and device-loss consequences are explicit for every strategy
validation: Browser capability checks on the supported matrix
Threat-model review against loss, sync, theft, and rollback
failureModes: Unsupported PRF never downgrades silently
Authentication-tag or envelope-version failures are terminal
KDF parameters are bounded against resource exhaustion

tasks.title: Implement the encrypted vault and IndexedDB adapter
tasks.objective: Implement credential encryption, authenticated metadata, indexing, deletion, corruption handling, and versioned IndexedDB migrations behind storage and crypto ports.
deliverables: In-memory and IndexedDB stores
AES-GCM versioned envelope with authenticated metadata
Migration, deletion, and corruption-recovery tests
acceptance: Raw credentials are never stored plaintext
Index metadata is minimized and documented
Tampering, partial writes, old versions, and failed migrations do not expose partial plaintext
validation: Fake IndexedDB migration and transaction tests
failureModes: Use atomic transactions for writes and migrations
Surface recoverable versus terminal vault errors
Never include decrypted credentials in exception messages

tasks.title: Implement the version-pinned SD-JWT VC adapter
tasks.objective: Wrap a maintained SD-JWT implementation for the pinned SD-JWT VC draft subset, including issuance, disclosure, key binding, issuer metadata, status references, and negative fixtures.
deliverables: Narrow issue, present, and verify adapter interfaces
Synthetic AgeCredential fixtures with is_over_18
Draft/version metadata and upgrade notes
acceptance: Undisclosed claims cannot be reconstructed from the presentation
Signature, digest, key-binding, algorithm, type, and expiry failures are rejected
Fixtures identify exact draft and media type behavior
validation: Official or upstream test vectors where license permits
Mutation tests for disclosures and JOSE headers
failureModes: Allowlist algorithms and key types
Bound token/disclosure sizes and counts
Fail closed on an unrecognized draft/profile version

tasks.title: Implement the OpenID4VCI issuance flow
tasks.objective: Implement the bounded OpenID4VCI 1.0 pre-authorized-code flow needed by the demo, with metadata validation, proof handling, and deterministic HTTP fixtures.
deliverables: Issuer metadata and credential-offer parsers
Wallet client state machine and issuer-side test adapter
Success, OAuth error, timeout, malformed metadata, and proof-failure fixtures
nonGoals: Every optional grant or wallet attestation
acceptance: The supported flow follows final 1.0 names and endpoints
Redirects and remote metadata obey SSRF/origin/size/time policies
The issued credential is verified before vault insertion
validation: Protocol unit tests with deterministic HTTP adapter
failureModes: Do not follow arbitrary redirects or private-network metadata URLs
OAuth errors map to safe user actions
Never persist an unverified credential as valid

tasks.title: Implement the OpenID4VP and DCQL presentation flow
tasks.objective: Implement the supported OpenID4VP 1.0 same-device request/response path using DCQL, direct_post, state/nonce, audience, holder binding, and strict disclosure selection.
deliverables: Wallet request parser and candidate selector
Verifier request builder and response verifier
Signed/request-URI trust hooks and negative protocol fixtures
acceptance: Wrong audience, nonce, state, holder key, response URI, and disclosure set are rejected
Only holder-approved claims enter the presentation
Replay state is consumed atomically
failureModes: Unknown transaction_data is rejected as required
Ambiguous verifier identity blocks consent
Mismatched or duplicate response parameters fail closed

tasks.title: Build the synthetic OpenID4VCI issuer demo
tasks.objective: Build a minimal issuer that creates a synthetic AgeCredential offer and issues a signed is_over_18 credential through the supported local OpenID4VCI flow.
deliverables: Issuer metadata, offer, token, credential, status, and public-key routes
Clearly synthetic fixture UI
Deterministic local signing-key lifecycle for tests
acceptance: A wallet can complete the supported offer flow
The UI never asks for or suggests real PII
Expired, reused, invalid-code, and revoked fixtures are testable
validation: OpenID4VCI contract test against the client package
failureModes: Test signing keys are unmistakably non-production
Errors do not expose tokens or signing material
Rate and size bounds exist even in the demo

tasks.title: Build the wallet web demo
tasks.objective: Build the wallet UI for local unlock, credential offer intake, verification-before-storage, encrypted listing/deletion, request review, disclosure approval, and presentation submission.
deliverables: Vault setup/unlock and credential lifecycle screens
OpenID4VCI intake and OpenID4VP consent flow
Actionable privacy-safe error states
acceptance: The UI shows issuer/verifier, purpose, expiry, requested and disclosed claims
No credential plaintext persists outside the unlocked session
Lock, delete, corrupt-vault, rejected-offer, and cancelled-presentation paths work
validation: Browser integration tests with fake IndexedDB/WebAuthn capabilities
Accessibility checks for the complete local flow
failureModes: Never auto-approve or silently disclose
Unsupported PRF presents the approved fallback
Sensitive data is redacted from logs and error boundaries

tasks.title: Build the OpenID4VP verifier demo
tasks.objective: Build a minimal verifier that generates a DCQL request for is_over_18, tracks state/nonce, validates the presentation off-chain, and grants a local demo session.
deliverables: Request and callback endpoints
Verification pipeline UI with safe reason codes
Single-use access-session result
acceptance: Only a fully valid presentation grants access
Every validation class has a tested rejection fixture
A rejection reveals no hidden claim-matching information
failureModes: Fail closed on unavailable trust/status data
Do not distinguish consent denial from claim mismatch in a privacy-leaking way
Never log the full vp_token

tasks.title: Integrate the deterministic local vertical slice
tasks.objective: Provide one command that starts the three local apps and proves issuance, encrypted storage, minimal presentation, off-chain verification, and access without chain or hosted infrastructure.
deliverables: Playwright happy path
Required negative and restart/persistence paths
Exact local runbook and test fixture reset
acceptance: The happy path passes from a clean data directory
No birthdate or undisclosed claim reaches the verifier
Signature, replay, expiry, status, holder-binding, and vault-tamper failures deny access
validation: Inspect network/log artifacts for secret and undisclosed-claim leakage
Repeat after app restart and fixture reset
failureModes: E2E does not paper over prerequisite failures
Ports and child processes are cleaned up reliably
Screenshots/traces are sanitized before retention

tasks.title: Select the smart-account base and build the Foundry harness
tasks.objective: Compare Safe and Kernel, select the maintained base, pin deployments and EntryPoint compatibility, and create a local Foundry/account-adapter harness without writing a custom account base.
deliverables: Decision ADR with license, audits, recovery, provider independence, and migration analysis
Pinned ABIs, chain/deployment manifest, and code-hash verification
Local account deployment and execution test harness
acceptance: The selected base satisfies ERC-1271 and has a credible ERC-4337/passkey path
Local deployments are deterministic and code hashes are asserted
Hosted SDK/provider dependencies are isolated behind the account adapter
failureModes: Reject incompatible EntryPoint/module combinations
Do not trust an address without chain ID and code hash
Document upgrade and module-install authority

tasks.title: Implement the local passkey smart account and ERC-1271 flow
tasks.objective: Register a WebAuthn passkey, derive or deploy the selected smart account locally, execute a local operation, and validate account signatures through ERC-1271.
deliverables: WebAuthn signer adapter with origin/RP/challenge checks
Counterfactual/deployed account flow on Anvil
ERC-1271 positive and negative contract tests
acceptance: Passkey private material never leaves the authenticator
Wrong origin, RP ID, challenge, signature, and account reject
Account address remains deterministic under the documented inputs
validation: Anvil integration and forge ERC-1271 tests
failureModes: Explicitly handle user cancellation and unavailable authenticators
P-256 verifier path is pinned and code-hash checked
Never conflate passkey assertion with vault decryption

tasks.title: Add the opt-in ERC-4337 testnet adapter
tasks.objective: Submit and observe a passkey-authorized UserOperation through configurable bundler/paymaster adapters on one documented testnet while preserving fully local core tests.
deliverables: Validated environment schema and provider-neutral ports
UserOperation simulation/submission/receipt flow
Testnet smoke runbook with chain and deployment manifest
acceptance: Missing external configuration cleanly skips opt-in tests
Simulation errors and sponsorship denial are actionable
A successful operation is linked to exact EntryPoint, chain, account, and receipt
failureModes: Never fall back to an unintended chain or RPC
Redact API credentials and signed payload diagnostics
Retry policy does not duplicate an already-included operation

tasks.title: Integrate and test the pinned ERC-7579 compatibility path
tasks.objective: Integrate the selected maintained ERC-7579 adapter, prove module install/use/remove behavior locally, and document Draft-standard migration risk.
deliverables: Pinned adapter and module manifest
Install, use, uninstall, and recovery tests
Compatibility ADR addendum
nonGoals: Writing a new modular account standard
acceptance: Account behavior remains valid before and after module lifecycle
Malicious/reverting module fixtures cannot silently seize control
Draft version and upgrade path are visible in runtime/deployment metadata
validation: Foundry module lifecycle and reentrancy tests
failureModes: Module uninstall denial has a documented recovery path
Fallback/hook authorization is fail-closed
No delegatecall target is accepted without explicit policy

tasks.title: Decide and implement DID control and holder binding
tasks.objective: Compare did:pkh and did:ethr for contract-account control, decide where DID is actually needed, and implement a privacy-aware holder-binding adapter that survives passkey rotation.
deliverables: DID/control/privacy ADR
Resolver and control-proof ports with deterministic fixtures
Credential-scoped or pairwise holder-binding strategy where supported
nonGoals: Universal resolver dependency in core tests
acceptance: Passkey rotation does not require a new public account identity
Base credential flow works with the DID adapter disabled
Correlation implications of every binding mode are documented and tested
validation: Privacy review of identifiers exposed to issuer and verifier
failureModes: Resolver outage is explicit and scoped
Contract-account signature verification uses the correct chain
No fallback silently replaces strong holder binding with bearer behavior

tasks.title: Implement issuer trust and credential status/revocation
tasks.objective: Implement a versioned local trust policy and the pinned status mechanism with bounded fetching, cache freshness, issuer key rotation, and deterministic revocation fixtures.
deliverables: Trust-bundle schema and policy evaluator
Status fetch/cache adapter and issuer demo endpoints
Valid, revoked, suspended, stale, unavailable, and rotated-key fixtures
nonGoals: Putting credential status or PII on-chain
acceptance: Revoked/suspended credentials are rejected
Unknown issuer and stale/unavailable status follow explicit fail-closed policy
Status lookup does not leak holder-specific identifiers
failureModes: No silent acceptance on network failure
Issuer key rotation cannot validate with an untrusted replacement key
Error copy distinguishes retryable infrastructure failure from invalid credential without leaking claims

tasks.title: Implement account recovery and encrypted vault backup/restore
tasks.objective: Provide tested signer rotation/account recovery and a separately authenticated encrypted vault export/restore flow, making their independent success conditions clear.
deliverables: Recovery policy and timelock/guardian or selected maintained module integration
Versioned encrypted backup envelope with KDF and integrity metadata
Lost-device, colluding-guardian, wrong-passphrase, rollback, and partial-recovery tests
acceptance: Recovered account keeps the documented stable address/control identity
A backup never contains plaintext credentials or keys
Account recovery without vault backup and vault restore without account control are handled honestly
failureModes: Timelock and guardian thresholds cannot be bypassed
Rollback/version downgrade is detected
Wrong recovery input does not reveal whether a credential exists

tasks.title: Harden consent, phishing resistance, and privacy UX
tasks.objective: Make request trust, verifier identity, purpose, exact disclosures, expiry, status, and denial behavior understandable while preventing silent or coercive presentation.
deliverables: Consent and risk-state interaction spec implemented in the apps
Signed/request-URI trust indicators and unsafe-request blockers
Privacy-safe denial and claim-mismatch behavior
acceptance: The holder can distinguish requester, requested data, shared data, purpose, and expiry
Unsafe or ambiguous requests cannot reach approval
Denial does not reveal whether hidden claims matched
failureModes: Never render remote metadata as trusted unsanitized HTML
No pre-checked consent or approval-by-timeout
Error details do not leak undisclosed claims

tasks.title: Build the short-lived on-chain attestation and access demo
tasks.objective: Convert a valid off-chain result into a short-lived attestor-signed, chain/consumer/policy/nonce-scoped message and gate one local/testnet demo contract without writing credential data on-chain.
deliverables: Versioned attestation envelope and signer/verifier interfaces
Consumer contract with expiry, nonce/nullifier, policy, audience, and attestor rotation checks
Access demo and privacy/trust documentation
acceptance: Only a valid scoped unexpired unused attestation grants access
Chain replay, consumer replay, nonce reuse, wrong policy, and rotated/revoked attestor reject
Events and calldata contain no credential, DID document, or PII
validation: Foundry unit, fuzz, replay, and gas tests
Local integration from verifier result to consumer
Opt-in testnet smoke if configuration exists
failureModes: Trust in the attestor is explicit and versioned
Attestor compromise has a rotation/revocation path
On-chain failure never changes the validity of the underlying off-chain credential

tasks.title: Add adversarial, property, fuzz, and redaction hardening
tasks.objective: Turn the threat model into automated adversarial evidence across parsers, JOSE, replay, vault, recovery, consent, status, modules, and logs.
deliverables: Cross-package property and mutation tests
Foundry fuzz/invariant suite
Structured redaction tests and sanitized failure artifacts
acceptance: Every initial threat has at least one test or documented manual control
Fuzz/property seeds are reproducible
Logs, traces, screenshots, and errors exclude secrets, credentials, and undisclosed claims
failureModes: Flaky randomized tests preserve failing seeds
No test uses real PII or production endpoints
A sanitizer failure fails CI rather than merely warning

tasks.title: Integrate the full local and testnet release candidate
tasks.objective: Run and document the complete synthetic flow locally and on the supported testnet, including account creation, credential exchange, recovery, status rejection, and optional attestation-gated access.
deliverables: Release-candidate orchestration command and environment validation
Browser/chain/provider support matrix
Acceptance report with artifacts and exact deployment manifest
acceptance: All local tests pass without external configuration
Opt-in testnet flow passes on the declared matrix
Recovery, revoked credential, provider outage, and attestation replay scenarios pass
validation: SBOM, license, secret, dependency, and contract code-hash checks
failureModes: Do not mark the RC green when any required criterion is skipped
Classify external outage separately from product defect
Artifacts are sanitized and reproducible

tasks.title: Prepare the independent security and privacy review packet
tasks.objective: Produce a reviewer-ready evidence packet covering assets, trust boundaries, key lifecycle, protocol profiles, contracts, deployments, privacy data flow, tests, known gaps, and reproducible setup.

Known-issues, scope, reproducibility, and reviewer checklist
acceptance: A reviewer can reproduce builds/tests from a clean clone

failureModes: Missing evidence is listed as a gap, not inferred
No secret is included in the packet
Threats without controls block production claims

tasks.title: Publish the first open-source alpha release
tasks.objective: After explicit release approval, publish a signed alpha tag and GitHub release with accurate maturity warnings, reproducible checks, artifacts, limitations, and no production-security claim.
deliverables: Versioned changelog and release notes
Signed tag and GitHub alpha release
Updated current-state and support documentation
acceptance: Release commit equals the verified RC source
Published artifacts and checksums are reproducible
Warnings clearly limit the alpha to synthetic data and local/testnet use
validation: Re-run release checks from the tag
Verify GitHub visibility, tag signature, checksums, and links
Inspect release archive for secrets and local artifacts
failureModes: Stop before external publication without explicit approval
Do not republish changed artifacts under the same tag

tasks.title: Research a future ZK predicate-proof path
tasks.objective: Evaluate whether a maintained, auditable proof system can prove hidden age predicates while binding issuer, status, holder, audience, nonce, expiry, and nullifier semantics.
deliverables: Comparison of candidate proof systems and circuit assumptions
Browser performance and on-chain cost measurements on synthetic fixtures
Go, defer, or reject ADR with a bounded implementation proposal
acceptance: Trusted setup, audit status, cryptographic assumptions, licensing, and maintenance are compared
Revocation and anti-replay binding are part of the design

validation: Independent review of the research assumptions
No product dependency added unless the ADR says go
failureModes: Do not select a proof system on gas cost alone
Do not claim unlinkability without a concrete transcript analysis
Abandon candidates that require custom unaudited cryptography for the MVP
